text.tspan: Two ways programs talk: client–server and peer-to-peer
browser → web server · kubectl → API server
The server holds the data: one place to manage,
Single point of failure, unless several servers
sit behind a load balancer · scales by adding servers
Roles, not machines: nginx is a server to browsers
and a client to the app behind it
Each peer is both client and server
Peers talk directly; no central server holds data
No single point of failure; new peers add capacity
Real systems mix them: a video call finds the other person through a server (signalling), sends audio and video
directly peer to peer, and falls back to a relay server when NAT blocks the direct path.
